The Panama Canal offers two distinct experiences in a single trip. At Miraflores, visitors watch ships passing through the locks and learn how the waterway works. On Gatun Lake, they travel between forested shores alongside the passage of large vessels.

The "Panama City and Gamboa" itinerary includes these experiences on separate days. First comes an introduction to the canal's history and operation, followed by a boat trip to Monkey Island. The forest around Gamboa reveals the natural side of the canal's waterways.

At the Panama Rainforest Discovery Center, visitors can discover the tropical forest at different heights. The experience begins on paths among the trees before climbing an observation tower. From the upper platform, the green forest canopy stretches into view.

The centre is located near Pipeline Road, close to Soberanía National Park. Its work focuses on ecotourism and environmental education linked to bird conservation. On the six-day itinerary, a walk along the trails and a climb up the tower form part of a day exploring the forests around Gamboa.

## The Panama Canal and Casco Viejo: what to see in Panama's capital

### Panama City: the capital of Panama!

Panama City brings together numerous buildings from the colonial era and a modern city of skyscrapers, business centres, shops and restaurants. Take a tour of the ruins of historic Panama Viejo. This area is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as is the San Felipe district, known as the Old Town.

The French Park, established by the French during the first attempt to build the Panama Canal, is particularly interesting, as is Ancon Park. Avenida Balboa stretches along the bay from San Felipe, linking the Old Town with the business district.

## Panama City: a city of contrasts!

The main shopping centres are near the Panama Canal Museum. The Bridge of the Americas, which spans the Panama Canal, was the only road connection between North and South America until 1962. Enjoy one of the city's finest pedestrian areas with a stroll along the Amador Causeway. Not far from Panama City is the famous Malibu Beach, where diving and surfing are possible. Metropolitan National Park lies near the Panama Canal. Visitors can enjoy seeing a wide variety of butterflies, parrots, toucans, reptiles, anteaters and other wildlife. An orchid exhibition features species found only in Panama. The viewing platform also offers a view of the Panama Canal.

## The first Panama City on the Pacific coast

Panama Viejo preserves traces of the city founded in 1519. Visitors can see foundations, the remains of public buildings and monasteries, and the stone tower of the former cathedral rising above them. The ruins offer a sense of the layout of an early colonial city.

After Henry Morgan's attack in 1671, the city was moved to the area now known as Casco Antiguo. Panama Viejo and Casco Viejo therefore represent different periods in the capital's history. They can easily be combined in one sightseeing tour.

We offer a visit to Panama Viejo as part of a city tour with an English-speaking guide. The entrance ticket is included in our six-hour group tour. We can discuss the arrangements for a separate visit when you book.

The Pantanal is a vast landscape of seasonally flooded plains, rivers and abundant wildlife. Travelers come here to watch birds, caimans, capybaras, giant otters, anteaters, anacondas and jaguars.

Daytime activities can include horseback riding, boat excursions and fishing. Staying on a Brazilian fazenda allows visitors to spend several days right in the region's natural surroundings.

After sunset, guests can head out on a jeep safari and try to spot animals that are more active at night.
